acsText.recordedWhenYouHold40~ae9691d8: Recorded when you hold 40–50° of bank in the air for at least 15 seconds — or whenever you fly one from the EFB's Training page.
acsText.hold45OfBankYour~8922b093: Hold 45° of bank — your average through the turn has to stay within 5° of it.
acsText.holdTheAltitudeYouRolled~cfe351c: Hold the altitude you rolled in at, within 100 ft.
acsText.stayInTheBankAt~a9ce6fe7: Stay in the bank at least 15 seconds, or the turn isn't picked up automatically.
acsText.recordedWhenYouFlyBetween~e47a31: Recorded when you fly between stall speed and 1.3× stall speed, airborne, for at least 30 seconds — or whenever you fly it from the EFB's Training page.
acsText.stayInThatSpeedBand~845ee124: Stay in that speed band for 30 seconds or more, or it isn't recorded.
acsText.holdTheAltitudeYouStarted~fd361d: Hold the altitude you started at, within 100 ft.
acsText.keepItCoordinatedAtLeast~b8966e3: Keep it coordinated — at least 80% of the time with the ball within 5°.
acsText.30SAtSlowFlight~f6fa7172: 30 s at slow-flight speed · altitude ±100 ft · heading ±10° · coordinated
acsText.needsTheAircraftSStall~3d54a2bc: Needs the aircraft's stall speed. Airframes GARealistic has no spec for are never picked up automatically — fly it from the EFB's Training page instead.
acsText.recordedTheMomentTheStall~811849: Recorded the moment the stall warning sounds in the air — power-on if the throttle is at 50% or more when it fires, power-off if it isn't.
acsText.reachARealStallThe~4dbb7c69: Reach a real stall — the warning has to fire.
acsText.recoverPromptlyLosingMoreThan~c0: Recover promptly — losing more than 100 ft costs points, more than 200 ft costs double.
acsText.stayCoordinatedThroughTheBreak~5: Stay coordinated through the break and the recovery, and hold your heading within 10°.
acsText.flyOutOfItProperly~de05ef3f: Fly out of it properly: recovery is measured to the point the warning clears with the aircraft climbing again.
acsText.reachTheStallRecoverInside~cdc85: Reach the stall · recover inside 100 ft, coordinated, on heading
acsText.recordedWhenYouFlyA~be02e72d: Recorded when you fly a complete circle — a full 360° of ground track at 60–130 kt, airborne, inside about 10 minutes.
acsText.finishTheLapAnythingUnder~a0dc15: Finish the lap. Anything under 350° isn't recorded.
acsText.holdTheRadiusStayingWithin~ee7d9: Hold the radius: staying within 20% of the circle you're actually flying scores full marks.
acsText.radiusAndBankAngleDon~14c30dc8: Radius and bank angle don't matter — a wide shallow orbit scores the same as a tight steep one. Only how round the track is counts.
acsText.aTrackMoreThan42~38adf428: A track more than 42% out of round isn't treated as a circle at all (that's what keeps holding patterns out of your training log).
acsText.oneFullLapRadiusHeld~0120b484: One full lap · radius held within 20% · any radius, any bank
acsText.recordedWhenYouFlyTwo~58e924b8: Recorded when you fly two 180° turns back to back in opposite directions, each finished within about 2½ minutes.
acsText.eachHalfHasToBe~b0ed6230: Each half has to be 170–190° of turn — rolling out early or carrying past 190° means it isn't recorded.
acsText.theSecondTurnHasTo~6908728b: The second turn has to reverse the first.
acsText.keepItCoordinatedTheScore~43bc18: Keep it coordinated — the score is the share of the maneuver flown with the ball within 5°.
acsText.recordedOnAnIfrFlight~acbdcea9: Recorded on an IFR flight plan when you fly a published approach into your destination, starting within 1 nm of one of its initial fixes.
acsText.keepTheNeedleCentred80~78718ce1: Keep the needle centred. 80% of the approach inside ¼ dot grades ATP, ½ dot Commercial, ¾ dot Instrument, 1 dot Private.
acsText.ilsApproachesAreGradedOn~c9523f6: ILS approaches are graded on localizer and glideslope; everything else on distance from the published track (1 dot ≈ 0.12 nm).
acsText.flyItToALanding~26f0046d: Fly it to a landing or fly the missed — the graded segment runs from the initial fix to touchdown or the go-around.
acsText.80OfTheApproachInside~ca9ae3d4: 80% of the approach inside ¼ dot = ATP · ½ = Commercial · ¾ = Instrument · 1 dot = Private
acsText.needsADestinationWithApproach~94: Needs a destination with approach procedures in the nav data, and an IFR flight plan.
acsText.recordedWhenYouPassOver~d9cad2e9: Recorded when you pass over a holding fix published on one of the approaches serving your landing runway at least twice, 1½ to 10 minutes apart — each pair of passes is graded as one circuit.
acsText.holdYourAltitudeInside50~0916e13: Hold your altitude — inside 50 ft is clean, past 100 ft costs 20 points.
acsText.turnThePublishedDirectionRight~5: Turn the published direction (right unless the procedure says left) — 25 points.
acsText.flyOneMinuteLegsSo~a9582bad: Fly one-minute legs, so a circuit takes about two minutes. More than 15 s out costs points, more than 30 s costs more.
acsText.comeBackOverTheFix~7e65de70: Come back over the fix — inside 0.3 nm is clean, past 0.5 nm costs 15 points.
acsText.altitude100FtCorrectTurn~3a79cc0: Altitude ±100 ft · correct turn direction · 1-minute legs · back over the fix inside 0.3 nm
acsText.measuredAutomaticallyFromEverySt: Measured automatically from every stretch of level flight (vertical speed inside ±200 fpm) outside the maneuvers above — you don't have to do anything to trigger it.
acsText.holdAltitudeWithin100Ft~b9c24bc1: Hold altitude within 100 ft of what you've been cruising at.
acsText.keepTurnsCoordinatedBallWithin~f: Keep turns coordinated — ball within 5° any time bank passes 10°.
acsText.levelCruiseHeldTo100~0188661a: Level cruise held to ±100 ft · ±10° heading · ±10 kt · coordinated in the turns
acsText.recordedAutomaticallyAfterAnyFli: Recorded automatically after any flight where SayIntentions.AI (AI-voiced ATC) was configured and running — nothing to trigger manually.
acsText.everyAtcInstructionShouldGet~270: Every ATC instruction should get an acknowledged pilot response — an instruction with no recorded reply counts against the score.
acsText.scoreReflectsHowMuchOf~5003dafb: Score reflects how much of the flight's radio traffic was answered, bucketed to the same ACS levels as every other task.
acsText.responseRateAcrossRecordedAtc~16: Response rate across recorded ATC transmissions, ATP 90+ down to Private 60+
acsText.flownFromTheEfbS~71a69a95: Flown from the EFB's Training page — line up on the runway (or start airborne on upwind) and fly four 90° turns round to final.
acsText.upwind20PtsTrackThe~54c5aabc: Upwind (20 pts): track the runway heading, within 10°.
acsText.crosswind20PtsTurnAt~bbcf050e: Crosswind (20 pts): turn at 15–30° of bank.
acsText.downwind25PtsHoldPattern~50b83c3: Downwind (25 pts): hold pattern altitude — 1,000 ft above where you started — within 100 ft.
acsText.base15PtsTurnAt~c3523bd9: Base (15 pts): turn at 15–30° of bank.
acsText.final20PtsLineUp~53d42969: Final (20 pts): line up with the runway within 10° and hold a steady approach speed.
acsText.gradedOnTheTablet95~fe76e56e: Graded on the tablet: 95+ ATP, 85+ Commercial, 75+ IFR, 65+ VFR.
acsText.levelComesFromTheScore~efc20f62: Level comes from the score: 90+ ATP · 80+ Commercial · 70+ Instrument · 60+ Private. Flying exactly at the ACS limits scores about 70 — flying them comfortably scores in the 90s.

acsText.steepTurnsTurnsAroundA~2def7906: Steep turns, turns around a point, S-turns.

acsText.attitudeInstrumentFlyingPartialP: Attitude instrument flying, partial panel, unusual attitudes.
acsText.steepTurnsAndStallsHeld~ed4baccc: Steep turns and stalls held to commercial tolerances.

acsText.soloCrossCountryDistanceAirport~: Solo cross-country distance/airport count is tracked cumulatively across all solo XC flights, not one single 150nm/3-point flight — Flight records one leg each.
acsText.picTimeIsApproximatedAs~50e97041: "PIC time" is approximated as total flight time once Private is held — GARealistic has no CFI concept to model real-world PIC-logging nuances.
acsText.picTimeApproximatedAsTotal~a6146: "PIC time" approximated as total flight time once Private is held; long-XC requirements use the same cumulative-distance simplification as PPL.
acsText.anAspirationalTierMostPlayers~c4: An aspirational tier — most players won't reach 1,500 hrs soon. PIC/class-time sub-splits are subsumed by the four tracked totals.
acsText.faaSetsNoFixedHour~65b68882: FAA sets no fixed hour minimum for the added class rating (proficiency + practical test only) — this is a GARealistic guideline, not an FAA minimum. A class rating is added to an existing certificate, so Private is required first (real-world, it's typically added well before Commercial/ATP, not after — Commercial actually requires complex/TAA time as one of its own prerequisites).
acsText.6131ERequiresTraining~ea849b8f: 61.31(e) requires training + a logbook endorsement, no fixed hour minimum — this is a GARealistic guideline, not an FAA minimum. The FARs don't actually require Private first (a student pilot can be endorsed), but GARealistic gates it there to stop a zero-hour pilot picking up an aircraft-type endorsement before a certificate.
acsText.6131FRequiresTraining~f4d0fa44: 61.31(f) requires training + a logbook endorsement, no fixed hour minimum — this is a GARealistic guideline, not an FAA minimum. The FARs don't actually require Private first (a student pilot can be endorsed), but GARealistic gates it there to stop a zero-hour pilot picking up an aircraft-type endorsement before a certificate.
acsText.6131GRequiresGround~1454fcf4: 61.31(g) requires ground training + a logbook endorsement, no fixed hour minimum — this is a GARealistic guideline, not an FAA minimum. The FARs don't actually require Private first (a student pilot can be endorsed), but GARealistic gates it there to stop a zero-hour pilot picking up an aircraft-type endorsement before a certificate.
acsText.6131IRequiresTraining~538eb293: 61.31(i) requires training + a logbook endorsement, no fixed hour minimum — this is a GARealistic guideline, not an FAA minimum. The FARs don't actually require Private first (a student pilot can be endorsed), but GARealistic gates it there to stop a zero-hour pilot picking up an aircraft-type endorsement before a certificate.
acsText.garealisticHasNoFloatplaneAmphib: GARealistic has no floatplane/amphibious aircraft classification, so this rating can't be auto-tracked — manual toggle only, same as today.
acsText.requiresASayintentionsAiSubscrip: Requires a SayIntentions.AI subscription and API key (Settings → Integrations). Advisory only — a pilot who never sets this up is never blocked from a certificate's Ready status over it.
acsText.soloFlightsOf50Nm~4eb7237c: Solo flights of 50 nm or more between two airports (straight-line distance; flights marked dual received don't count). Needs 5 hours, 150 nm in total and 3 airports.

guide.thisIsHomeBaseAircraftStatus: This is home base — aircraft status, quick-launch to MSFS, and your pre-flight tools all live here. Let's take a quick tour of the app.
guide.importAircraftFromMsfsViewThem: Import aircraft from MSFS, view them on a map, or scatter rentals near your base. Each aircraft row has Status, Configuration, Purchase and Sell. Configuration includes the POH tab — check it to make sure its performance specs are accurate.
guide.theAircraftMarketHasAWeekly: The Aircraft Market has a weekly board of new and used listings. A used aircraft's condition is fixed the moment it's listed — pay for a Pre-Buy Inspection before you buy if you want to know its real condition, not just what the seller discloses.
guide.trackEverythingYouOwnBeyondThe: Track everything you own beyond the flight line — hangars, tools, and other property tied to your operation.
guide.checkOffTheCertificatesAndRatings: Check off the certificates and ratings you actually hold — it's an honor system. Each one has currency requirements tracked from your logged flights. Prefer not to track this? Turn off endorsement warnings in Settings.
guide.asYouFlyYoullUnlockAchievements: As you fly, you'll unlock achievements that measure your accomplishments. Come back here any time to track progress and view the achievement map.
guide.aReadinessScorecardForPplIr: A readiness scorecard for PPL/IR/CPL/ATP, built automatically from your best-ever graded performance on each required task — see exactly what's left before you'd be ready for a checkride.
guide.everyGradedManeuverApproachAndHold: Every graded maneuver, approach, and hold shows up here as you fly, alongside your endorsement sign-offs — a running record of your training, not just your logbook totals.
guide.everyFlightIsRecordedAutomatically: Every flight is recorded automatically — Hobbs time, night time, landings, approaches, even an ACS grade. There's nothing to press while you fly.
guide.trackEveryCostAndSourceOf: Track every cost and source of income. Click Add Income to log a recurring salary or a one-off deposit; Expenses and Obligations show what GA ownership really costs.
guide.flyCargoAndCharterJobsTo: Fly cargo and charter jobs to earn virtual income and build your charter reputation as you go.
guide.browseNearbyAirportsWithRunwayData: Browse nearby airports with runway data, community fuel prices, on-field amenities, and mechanics with their specialties and rates. Pick one and click Plan to build a flight to it. Feeling ambitious? The Scenery Editor here lets you place buildings and draw taxiways to generate a real MSFS scenery package for any airport.
guide.yourPlannedRouteLandsHereWith: Your planned route lands here, with SimBrief integration. Get familiar with the options before you file and fly.
guide.theTripPlannerBuildsMultiLeg: The Trip Planner builds multi-leg journeys by theme, distance and fuel stops — a great way to discover flights you'd never have planned yourself.
guide.readyForMoreFoundACompany: Ready for more? Found a company to run cargo and passenger routes, hire staff, and manage finances at a larger scale. Founding capital is a one-way door — personal money can never flow back into a company once it's founded, only dividends flow out.
guide.notReadyToOwnSoloShare: Not ready to own solo? Share one aircraft's costs with a small group instead. A Syndicate gives you an equal equity share you'd need to sell to leave; a Club is dues-only with no ownership stake. Which one a group picks is locked in at founding.
guide.notReadyToFoundYourOwn: Not ready to found your own company? Fly for hire under an existing employer's operation instead — a lighter-weight way to earn charter and cargo income.
guide.backHomeSelectYourAircraftAnd: Back home. Select your aircraft and run Prepare Flight to prep it, then launch MSFS when you're ready.
guide.thatsTheTourLoadUpIn: That's the tour. Load up in MSFS and fly — GARealistic records everything automatically. Welcome aboard!
guide.useImportMsfsToPullIn: Use Import MSFS to pull in an aircraft you already have installed, or add one by hand from the Aircraft tab. Set Ownership to Owned so purchase, loan, and insurance costs start tracking against it.
guide.openTheAircraftsPohAndCheck: Open the aircraft's POH and check its V-speeds, fuel capacity, and performance numbers against the real aircraft. Wrong numbers here throw off wear, training grades, and fuel planning everywhere else in the app.
guide.configurationForThisAircraftTheMtb: Configuration for this aircraft — the MTBF tab lets you add, remove, or retune individual components, and Variables maps custom gauges MSFS doesn't already recognize. Stock defaults are fine to start with; come back once you know the aircraft better. Base Airport (on the same screen) is where it lives between flights.
guide.backOnTheDashboardThePreflight: Back on the Dashboard, the Preflight Walkaround card checks fuel water, oil, tire pressure, and brake fluid — the small things that quietly fail an engine or blow a tire if you never check them. Fix anything it flags before you fly.
guide.runPrepareFlightToPrepThe: Run Prepare Flight to prep the aircraft, then launch MSFS. Everything else — Hobbs time, wear, training grades — is recorded automatically once you're in the air.
guide.addItFromTheAircraftTab: Add it from the Aircraft tab the same way as an owned aircraft, but leave Ownership set to Rental — you'll pay a per-hour rental rate instead of purchase, loan, and insurance costs, and the FBO handles its long-term upkeep between your sessions.
guide.openThePohAndCheckIts: Open the POH and check its V-speeds and performance numbers — a rental you didn't configure yourself is exactly as likely to have wrong POH data as one you imported.
guide.baseAirportInConfigurationIsWhere: Base Airport (in Configuration) is where you'll find this aircraft parked between flights — set it to the field you're actually renting from.
guide.aRentalsDayToDayWear: A rental's day-to-day wear is simulated between your sessions and the FBO fixes anything that drops too low for free — but the Preflight Walkaround card (fuel water, oil, tires, brakes) still reflects real condition on any given day. Check it before you fly.
guide.browseDestinationsForAirportsWithi: Browse Destinations for airports within range — filter by fuel price, amenities, and mechanic specialty. Click Plan on one to send it straight to Flight Planning.
guide.flightPlanningOpensWithYourAircraf: Flight Planning opens with your aircraft's current location as the origin automatically. Add your destination, and Insert Airway or SimBrief can fill in the enroute portion for you.
guide.windsAloftAndTheFuelPlanning: Winds Aloft and the fuel planning panel use real weather for whatever time you're planning around — refresh them if you change the route or departure time significantly.
guide.headBackToTheDashboardRun: Head back to the Dashboard, run Prepare Flight, and launch MSFS — the route you built is what SimBrief and the EFB will show once you're in the cockpit.
guide.theJobsBoardIsSizedTo: The Jobs board is sized to your aircraft and pilot reputation — higher reputation unlocks jobs farther from home. Accept one that fits your aircraft's range and payload.
guide.clickPlanJobOnTheAccepted: Click Plan Job on the accepted job — it jumps straight to Flight Planning with the job's origin and destination already filled in.
guide.addAnyWaypointsOrAirwaysYou: Add any waypoints or airways you want, check winds and fuel, then you're ready to fly the leg.
guide.flyItAndCompleteTheJob: Fly it and complete the job
guide.runPrepareFlightLaunchMsfsAnd: Run Prepare Flight, launch MSFS, and fly it. A hard landing costs part of the payout — separate from any component wear it causes — so land it smoothly.
guide.theAircraftMarketRefreshesWeeklyWi: The Aircraft Market refreshes weekly with new and used listings. Filter by make, distance from your home base, and price to narrow it down.
guide.aUsedListingsConditionWasFixed: A used listing's condition was fixed the moment it appeared — buying it doesn't change that. Pay for a Pre-Buy Inspection to see the real condition before you buy, not just what the seller discloses.
guide.buyCommitsThePurchaseImmediatelyTh: Buy commits the purchase immediately — there's no cooling-off period, so inspect first if the condition matters to you.
guide.aUsedAircraftParkedAwayFrom: A used aircraft parked away from your base doesn't teleport to you — fly it home yourself if you can load that type in MSFS, or pay for a ferry contract from the purchase confirmation.
guide.makeSureYouCanActuallyFly: Make sure you can actually fly it
guide.youNeedThisAircraftTypeInstalled: You need this aircraft type installed in MSFS to fly it yourself and log real flights on it — buying a type you can't load only makes sense for a company-owned, AI-flown aircraft.
guide.theClubsTabListsSyndicatesAnd: The Clubs tab lists Syndicates and Clubs looking for members. Applying to join is single-member approval, not a vote — an existing member reviews and admits you directly.
guide.nothingLooksRightFoundOneInstead: Nothing looks right? Found one instead. The choice between the two is made once and can't be changed afterward: a Syndicate gives every member an equal equity share in one aircraft, a Club is dues-only with no ownership stake.
guide.knowWhatYoureSigningUpFor: Know what you're signing up for
guide.fallingBehindOnDuesHasReal: Falling behind on dues has real consequences for the whole group, not just you — other members front your share and are owed that money directly. Leaving a Syndicate means selling your equity share, not just walking away.
guide.bookAndFlyTheSharedAircraft: Book and fly the shared aircraft
guide.onceYoureInReserveTheShared: Once you're in, reserve the shared aircraft on the booking calendar, then check it out. You still need the same endorsements and currency you'd need to fly that aircraft on your own — membership doesn't waive training requirements.

guide.start.menu: I'm new - what do I do?
guide.start.sim.title: 1. Start the simulator
guide.start.sim.message: Load Microsoft Flight Simulator into a flight. GARealistic finds the sim by itself, so there is nothing to set up. The Getting started card on this page always shows the next step.
guide.start.aircraft.title: 2. Add your aircraft
guide.start.aircraft.message: Everything here, from costs to wear to your logbook, belongs to an aircraft. Import the one you have loaded in MSFS.
guide.start.home.title: 3. Set your home base
guide.start.home.message: Type the ICAO code of the airport you fly from in the Profile tab. Jobs, rentals and the Suggested Next Flight are built around it.
guide.start.job.title: 4. Pick something to fly
guide.start.job.message: Not sure where to go? Use Quick Flight on the Dashboard, or choose a job here and press Plan Job. You can also browse Destinations and build your own route in Flight Planning.
guide.start.prepare.title: 5. Prepare, then fly
guide.start.prepare.message: Select your aircraft and run Prepare Flight. After that, fly as normal. The flight starts and stops logging on its own, so there is no button to press.
guide.start.logbook.title: 6. See what it recorded
guide.start.logbook.message: After you land, the flight is in your Logbook, with its costs and any job pay in Finances. That is the whole loop: pick a flight, prepare, fly, review. Everything else in the sidebar can wait.
guide.start.web.title: Want more detail?
guide.start.web.message: Every page has a How this page works link above its content that opens the matching section of the web guide. Help also has a full written guide.

persistence.checksWhichControlsOnThisAir: Checks which controls on this aircraft the sim will actually let us put back between sessions. settings.companyDispatchPersonaOptionalN: Company dispatch persona (optional, needs a Company): a separate Virtual Airline key from SayIntentions support lets your company's name and current flight reach their AI dispatcher. Leave blank if you don't have one.
settings.scalesPersonalAndCompanyCostsAn: Scales personal and Company costs and thins the job board. Changing this takes effect on the next job-board refresh and billing pass — nothing already posted or charged is rewritten retroactively.
settings.affectsFuelQuantitiesAndWeights: Affects fuel quantities and weights throughout the app. Engine temperatures, pressure, and RPM always use their natural aviation units. Distance has its own setting below.
settings.whenEnabledEachFlightAccumulate: When enabled, each flight accumulates wear on aircraft components (engine, brakes, landing gear, avionics). Disable for casual flying or if you want to manage component health manually.
settings.whenEnabledTheAircraftStatusPag: When enabled, the Aircraft Status page and Repair Components dialog stop showing live component wear — only the last paid mechanic inspection's findings. Pay for an inspection at a mechanic to reveal current condition and get cost-to-fix options. Doesn't apply to A2A, Black Square, or SWS Kodiak aircraft, which manage their own wear.
settings.whenYouRegisterOrBuyAn: When you register or buy an aircraft of a type you've never saved your own POH/Variables/MTBF reference for (Configuration → POH/Variables/MTBF → "Save as My Reference"), this decides where it seeds its starting data from. Your own saved reference for that type — once you have one — always wins regardless of this setting.
settings.allMonetaryValuesPayoutsCostsFu: All monetary values (payouts, costs, fuel prices) are stored in USD and converted at a fixed rate. The currency is read once at launch, so a restart is needed to apply a change.
settings.distancesLogbookPilotStatsDesti: Distances (Logbook, Pilot Stats, Destinations, routes) are stored in nautical miles and converted at a fixed rate. Read once at launch, so a restart is needed to apply a change.
settings.whenEnabledAPopupIsShown: When enabled, a popup is shown at engine start if conditions are IMC or MVFR, prompting you to check your IFR clearance or local minimums.
settings.optionalGoNoGoThresholdsChecked: Optional go/no-go thresholds checked when you click Begin Flight. Leave a field blank to skip that check. Like the other preflight checks, this is a soft warning you can override — not a hard block.
settings.theSetupWizardAndGuidedDashboar: The setup wizard and guided dashboard tour shown to new pilots. Uncheck the box below to replay the guided tour the next time you launch GARealistic.
settings.darkIsTheDefaultAndIs: Dark is the default and is easier on the eyes in a night cockpit. Light suits a bright room or a second monitor next to the sim. A restart is needed to apply a change.
settings.garealisticChecksForANewRelease: GARealistic checks for a new release on startup and downloads it in the background — nothing installs until you click "Update & Restart" on the dashboard banner, and never while a flight is active.
settings.whenAnOwnedAircraftLoadsRestore: When an owned aircraft loads, restore its last-parked fuel and cockpit switches, and offer to move it back to where it was parked. Turn off to keep whatever MSFS loads. Your parked state is still recorded, so turning this back on picks up from the latest.
settings.servesASmallLocalWebPage: Serves a small local web page with live flight instruments — add it as an OBS Browser Source to show your stats on stream. Runs on your machine only (localhost); nothing is exposed to the internet.
settings.whenEnabledGarealisticRequiresT: When enabled, GARealistic requires the MSFS ATC tail number to match your registered aircraft's registration before it will track that aircraft. Disable this if you don't want to update the ATC ID in MSFS each time you switch aircraft — the app will then match by aircraft type only.
settings.whenEnabledHeliportsAirportsWit: When enabled, heliports (airports with no fixed-wing runways) are included in the Destinations and Jobs tabs. Each tab shows an additional filter checkbox so you can toggle heliport visibility independently. When disabled, heliports are always excluded (default for fixed-wing GA use). Independent of the Seaplane Bases option below. Changes take effect after saving and restarting the app.
settings.whenEnabledSeaplaneWaterOnlyBas: When enabled, seaplane/water-only bases (every runway is a water surface) are included in the Jobs tab, Trip Planner and Company cargo/freight boards. When disabled (default), they are always excluded, same as a heliport. Independent of Helicopter Mode above. Changes take effect after saving and restarting the app.
settings.whenEnabledJobWeightWarningsAre: When enabled, job weight warnings are shown in the planning modal but do not block acceptance. Disable to strictly enforce aircraft max gross weight limits.
settings.whenEnabledOnlyJobsOriginatingF: When enabled, only jobs originating from your tracked location below are acceptable — jobs elsewhere are still shown, but marked "fly there first." Your location updates automatically to the arrival airport whenever you complete a flight in any aircraft.
settings.clickSendLogToSubmitYour: Click Send Log to submit your current session log directly to the developer's bug-report channel — no account or setup required. The log contains only app events and aircraft info, no personal data. The webhook URL is pre-configured; you can override it below if needed.
settings.checksTheLinkToTheIn: Checks the link to the in-sim EFB tablet app: where the EFB add-on was found, whether its version matches this app, whether MSFS will serve the data files, and whether the EFB app has reported back. Run it with MSFS running and the GARealistic app open on the tablet for the most complete result. The full report is written to the session log, so send that log if you need help.
settings.setThePathToFlightsimulatorExe: Set the path to FlightSimulator.exe for each MSFS version you have installed, so the "Launch MSFS" buttons on the dashboard can start them. Use Detect to search automatically, or Browse to locate it manually. The Microsoft Store edition of MSFS 2024 has no exe — Detect stores a "STORE:" entry and launches it via the Windows shell.
settings.folderWhereMsfsSavesPlnFlight: Folder where MSFS saves .pln flight plan files. Used as the default location when browsing for plans on the SimBrief tab. Click Detect to auto-locate based on your MSFS install type (Store/Steam/Xbox Game Pass).
settings.onlyNeededIfYourAddOns: Only needed if your add-ons are installed outside the default Store/Steam location (e.g. relocated to another drive via UserCfg.opt InstalledPackagesPath, or a linked Community folder). Point this at your Packages folder — the one that contains the Community and Official folders — and the aircraft and add-on-airport scanners will search here first. Leave blank to auto-detect.
settings.whenEnabledAGoogleEarthKml: When enabled, a Google Earth (.kml) flight-track file is automatically saved to the folder below at the end of every flight. Choose below which clickable markers it carries alongside the track — flying repeatedly out of one field stacks them all on the same apron.
settings.airportData85000AirportsVors: Airport data (85,000+ airports, VORs, NDBs) is bundled with the app and updated silently in the background on each launch. No action required.
settings.onlyRequiredIfYouHaveInstalled: Only required if you have installed custom scenery or add-on airports that you want to appear in the Destinations list. Default airports are already included in the bundled data above. Requires an active MSFS connection. Supports both MSFS 2024 and MSFS 2020.
settings.powersTheFlightPlanningTabsAirw: Powers the Flight Planning tab's airway picker and route optimizer. Scans both MSFS 2020 and MSFS 2024 (whichever are installed, Microsoft Store or Steam) plus each sim's Community folder for add-on navigation data — all directly from disk, so no MSFS connection is required. Re-run after installing new scenery or updating the sim to pick up anything new — every run re-reads all of it, since resolving one fix's airway connections can depend on another fix defined in a completely different file, so it can take a while on a heavily-modded install. It opens in its own progress window so you can keep using Settings (or cancel) while it runs.
settings.preCachesRunwayFrequencyAndAppr: Pre-caches runway, frequency, and approach data from MSFS so it is available instantly for any airport. Requires an active MSFS connection. Runs one airport at a time in the background and can be cancelled at any time.
settings.msfsProcessesOneAirportAtA: MSFS processes one airport at a time. A full build may take several hours. Run it overnight or in the background while flying. Progress is preserved if you close the app — re-running only fetches airports not yet cached.
settings.controlsHowRentalAircraftAreSca: Controls how rental aircraft are scattered around your home base airport. Each scatter run adds up to the maximum number of aircraft at airports within the specified radius, preferring Community-folder addon airports.
settings.signInToShareLiveFlight: Sign in to share live flight positions, browse the community logbook, and claim your aircraft registration globally.
settings.actionsInThisTabArePermanent: Actions in this tab are permanent and cannot be undone.
settings.recomputesFlightTimeAndDepartur: Recomputes flight time and departure/arrival airports for past flights from their own recorded track, and rescales landing-gear positions recorded before v1.19.5. Use this if a flight shows engine (Hobbs) hours but 0.00 flight time, an arrival airport that doesn't match its map, or a landing report that fails its gear check at "1%" on an approach you flew with the gear down. Only flights showing that problem are touched — correct entries are never rewritten, and flights with no recorded track can't be recovered this way (edit those in the Logbook by hand). Corrected flights are re-uploaded to the community logbook automatically.
settings.pushesAllYourCompletedLocalFlig: Pushes all your completed local flights back to the community logbook. Use this after deleting online data to restore your community history, or to recover from a broken sync. Already-synced flights are safely overwritten with the latest local data — no duplicates.
settings.oneClickCorrectionWipesYourComm: One-click correction: wipes your community flight logbook, then re-uploads every completed local flight fresh from this PC. Use it when the online logbook shows wrong data (e.g. an arrival airport that matches the departure). Your aircraft registrations are kept and your local logbook is NOT affected.
settings.theReverseOfResyncReplacesYour: The reverse of Resync: replaces your local flight logbook with the copy stored online. Use it after a reinstall or on a new PC to get your flights back. Your local flights and paths are deleted first, then every flight in your cloud logbook is downloaded. Aircraft, expenses and settings are NOT affected. Flight paths, weather and grading aren't stored online, so only the logbook summary is restored.
settings.permanentlyDeletesYourPersonalA: Permanently deletes your personal aircraft, flights, expenses, and obligations. Company-fleet aircraft and your company are kept — use "Delete Company Data" below to remove those. Your airport database is preserved — no rebuild needed. When signed in, also removes your community flight records, live position, and aircraft registrations from the server.

start.sim.title: Start Microsoft Flight Simulator

start.home.why: Your base airport anchors jobs, rentals and the Suggested Next Flight, even when MSFS is closed. Type its ICAO code on the Profile tab.
start.fly.title: Fly your first flight
start.fly.why: Pick a job or plan a route, run Prepare Flight from the Dashboard, then fly. The flight logs itself, with Hobbs time, costs and wear.

start.simbrief.why: Enter your SimBrief pilot ID to pull your dispatch flight plans straight into Flight Planning.
